host.name: zbook
host.gpu: AMD Radeon 8060S (gfx1151, Ryzen AI MAX+ 395, 40 CU, unified LPDDR5X)
host.note: Every figure is gfx1151. No gfx1100 hardware was available.

change: The per-tile maximum walked the tile's shared-memory scores one float at a time -- 128 requests per row, in a single dependent fmax chain. It now reads four entries per instruction into four independent accumulators and combines them, with the scalar walk kept for a head_dim that is not a multiple of four. A max over a set is exact and order-independent for finite scores, which the projections and BF16 K/V guarantee, so this is bit-exact.
why: With the loads packed and eight rows per block, the kernel is instruction-issue-bound at roughly 75% of the issue limit rather than traffic-bound: rocprofv3 --pmc measures a 94% L2 hit rate and negligible DRAM traffic, so only fewer instructions or shorter chains can move it.

paired_kernel_ab.command: python3 scripts/yue2_attention_bench.py --repeat 8, alternating the two sources in one session
paired_kernel_ab.note: Absolute per-call times drift about 10% between batches on this host (the same sources measure 27.4-28.5 ms in a later batch), so only the paired ratio is claimed.

paired_replay_ab.command: python3 scripts/yue2_e2e_gate.py --only mandarin-off-s1234 --steps 2 --skip-live, alternating the two sources

rows_per_block_recheck.conclusion: Eight rows stays the optimum; the shorter maximum chain does not make sixteen rows viable, because the accumulation and weights work still scales with the row count.

bit_parity.result: bit-identical to the parent kernel (max abs diff 0.0)

next_candidates: The accumulation loop still reads eight shared-memory weights per key, which four-key groups would turn into two; the kernel is issue-bound, so that is the next measurable instruction cut.

Beyond that, the remaining gap to the pinned upstream at the product's 32 steps needs the register-blocked layout (a lane holding several keys' dot products) rather than more loop surgery, and that changes arithmetic so it needs the profile gates rather than bit parity.
